title: Quarterly Account Synopsis — Deckpack Templates (Standard & Enterprise)
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, adaptable deck pack for Quarterly Account Reviews (QARs) that scales from a lean Standard presentation (customer-facing, product-lite accounts) to an extended Enterprise variant (technical deep-dive, renewal negotiation focus). The goal is one canonical skeleton that CS reps can quickly tailor per account class, while preserving consistent signals for renewal playbooks and cross-org alignment.

Intended audience and outcomes:
- Primary: Customer Success Manager (CSM) + renewal lead.
- Secondary: Solutions Engineer, Account Executive (for renewal asks), Product PM (for roadmap signals).
- Outcomes: align on adoption & impact, surface risks early, agree next 90-day plan and renewal intent.

High-level guidance (how to use this pack):
- Use Standard pack for accounts < $60k ARR or low integration complexity. Keep to 10 slides / 20 minutes + 10 minutes Q&A.
- Use Enterprise pack for accounts >= $60k ARR or those with complex infra/integrations: 18–24 slides, allow 40–60 minutes (exec + technical tracks).
- Always populate the Renewal Tracker slide before the meeting (snapshot from CRM + telemetry).
- Speaker notes should include 2–3 tailored anecdotes or outcomes specific to the customer (do not read bullets verbatim).

---
Standard Deck (recommended skeleton — 10 slides)
1) Cover + Meeting goals (1 slide)
   - Title: Quarterly Account Synopsis – [Customer name]
   - Meeting goals: 3 bullets: confirm impact, surface blockers, agree next steps
   - Speaker note: call out any pre-meeting asks (e.g., decision needed).

2) Executive TL;DR (1 slide)
   - One-sentence health summary (green/amber/red) + top-line usage and ARR trend
   - Key wins since last QAR (3 bullets)

3) Adoption Snapshot (1 slide)
   - MAU/DAU (or relevant usage metric), feature adoption heatmap, retention cohort trend
   - Visual: sparkline + heatmap; include 90/30-day comparison

4) Value Realized (1 slide)
   - Concrete customer outcomes: time saved, automation volume, revenue-influence stats
   - Pull 1–2 customer quotes or success metrics

5) Health & Risk Overview (1 slide)
   - Health score (composite), top 3 risks, root causes, severity level
   - Speaker note: highlight any upcoming contract milestones that increase risk

6) Current Roadblocks & Support Requests (1 slide)
   - Open tickets > 30d, feature gaps, integration blockers, SLO incidents

7) Renewal Snapshot (1 slide)
   - Renewal date, ARR, recommended renewal approach (auto, discuss, escalate), CS-owned next step
   - Include CRM link and billing contact

8) 90-Day Plan (1 slide)
   - Ownership table: Quick wins (0–30d), Medium items (30–60d), Strategic (60–90d)

9) Asks & Decision Points (1 slide)
   - Pricing options (if applicable), support model changes, product roadmap asks

10) Appendix pointers + Next steps (1 slide)
   - Record follow-up owners, dates, and links to playbook checklists

---
Enterprise Deck (extended — recommended skeleton, 18 slides)
(Use when there are technical stakeholders, multi-product integrations, or a renewal negotiation in the quarter.)
1–3) Cover + Exec TL;DR + Strategic alignment (3 slides)
4) Business value deep-dive (2 slides)
5) Usage & performance by workload (2 slides)
6) Latency/cost/availability metrics (1 slide)
   - If the customer runs inference in Dedicated/Private modes, include per-model latency P95/P99 and token-cost trends
7) Integration topology + ownership map (1–2 slides)
8) Incident history and RCA status (1 slide)
9) Health & risk breakdown by domain (product, infra, org adoption) (1 slide)
10) Renewal economics & options (2 slides)
   - Scenarios: renew at current T&Cs, expanded seat/throughput contract, pilot to Dedicated
11) Proposed rollout and sequencing (1 slide)
12) Technical deep dives / performance tuning items (2 slides)
13) Customer asks backlog & product requests (1 slide)
14) SLA & operations (1 slide)
15) Final ask and signature slide (1 slide)

Speaker notes guidance (enterprise):
- For technical slides, include exact query to run for metrics, sample logs to show root cause, or shell commands for reproducing issues.
- Preface exec slides with business impact: every technical detail should connect to $$, time saved, or risk reduction.

Renewal Tracker (standalone slide template)
- Fields (present on a single slide): Renewal date; Contract ARR; Renewal owner; Renewal stage (intro, negotiating, committed); Last contact date; Health score; Adoption index; Top 3 blockers; Next 3 actions + owner; Escalation required? (Y/N).
- Visual: use colored status chip (G/A/R) and a tiny timeline (milestones).

Risk scoring matrix (one-pager to include in appendix)
- Inputs: usage delta (30d), support latency (avg time to close), NPS/CSAT snippets, business-critical feature coverage, exec sponsorship presence
- Combine into 0–100 score buckets: 0–40 (High risk), 41–70 (Moderate), 71–100 (Healthy)

Pre-meeting checklist (what CSM should do 2 weeks -> 1 day before):
- T-14d: Pull telemetry dashboard, confirm owners, draft agenda, invite attendees (exec + technical separately if enterprise).
- T-7d: Fill Renewal Tracker, attach product screenshots/graphs, validate contract terms with finance.
- T-3d: Share pre-read with customer (2 slide TL;DR + ask list).
- T-1d: Internal run-through w/ SE + AE (10–15 minutes).

Run-of-show templates (timing suggestions)
- Standard: 5m cover, 5m TL;DR, 8m adoption, 5m value, 5m risks, 5m plan, 7m Q&A
- Enterprise: 10m cover & exec alignment, 10m value, 10m infra/perf, 10m renewal economics, 10m technical deep dive, 10m actions & next steps

Playbook snippets (if health score drops below threshold)
- Early-warning (score 50–70): schedule health check, offer enablement workshop, propose targeted success plan (30–60d).
- Mid-risk (30–50): bring SE into calls, prioritize SLA guarantees, propose credit/discount pilot for a short remediation window.
- High-risk (<30): involve CRO + customer exec sponsor, create formal remediation plan with weekly checkpoints, consider pause of auto-renew prompts.

Assets & data sources (where to populate slides)
- Usage & adoption: telemetry dashboards (Looker/Grafana path), sample queries included in appendix.
- Support: Zendesk/GH issues > 30d link and summary line.
- Finance/Contract: CRM/Billing link + latest Order Form snapshot.

Visual guidance (keep consistent across accounts)
- Use one-line sparklines for trends (30/90 day), color by customer status (green/amber/red).
- Enterprise: when showing latency or cost figures, always include baseline + change % vs prior quarter and the unit cost per token/operation.

Follow-up & tracking cadence (post-meeting)
- Within 24 hours: CSM to send meeting notes, owner table, and calendar invites for action items.
- Weekly: automated renewal tracker update (shared sheet) until renewal is closed.
- Escalation: if any critical action misses owner deadline, trigger an escalation email to the AE lead and CS director (template in appendix).

Appendix: quick templates
- Exec script (30–60s): "We’ve seen X% growth in [key metric], which maps to Y hours saved for your team. Our ask today is to agree on the next-phase scope to bring that benefit to the next 3 teams."
- Technical script (30–60s): "We measured P95 latency of X ms on model Y under your typical payload; improvement plan A will reduce tail latency and lower per-call cost by Z%."

Unresolved items / TODOs (notes to self)
- Add lookup query for Dedicated-per-model token cost (SE to provide example by 2026-03-08).
- Finalize visuals for Renewal Economics scenarios (pricing team input).
- Build a one-click export from CRM->Renewal Tracker slide (automation request filed: JIRA-CH-4821).

Meeting hygiene (small reminders)
- Record the call (with permission) and timestamp the slide transitions for easy clip sharing.
- For enterprise meetings, always include an explicit 5-minute buffer for the exec sponsor to join late.

Contact & versioning
- Owner: Jordan Patel (CS) — jordan.patel@redwood.ai
- Template version: v0.7-draft

Notes to reviewers:
- This pack should be copied into a customer-specific folder and renamed to include account name + date. Keep the Renewal Tracker slide as a living single-source-of-truth and reference it in the CRM entry.
- Comments welcome — especially on the pricing scenarios and the risk-weighting function.
